The lithiation of (ferrocenylmethoxy)allene followed by sequential reaction with isothiocyanate and S- 
alkylation of the adduct gives the corresponding alkyl buta-2,3-dienimidothioate (1-aza-1,3,4-triene), 
which in the presence of CuI or CuBr cyclizes into (ferrocenylmethoxy)/sulfanyl-substituted pyrrole 
ring. The process is carried out in one or two preparative steps depending on an alkylating agent. A 
novel unexpected rearrangement of the synthesized 3-(ferrocenylmethoxy)-2-sulfanyl-1 H -pyrroles into 2- 
(ferrocenylmethyl)-2-sulfanyl-1,2-dihydro-3 H -pyrrol-3-ones, proceeding in CDCl 3 at room temperature or 
in toluene under heating, is discovered. The transformation of the 3-(ferrocenylmethoxy)-1 H -pyrroles into 
1,2-dihydro-3 H -pyrrol-3-ones is most likely the result of the formal [1,3]-O-to-C-rearrangements (acid- 
induced or thermal, respectively).

1. Introduction 
Both ferrocenes [1] and pyrroles [2] are among the well-known 
and the most popular classes of ﬁve-membered cyclic compounds, 
namely metallocenes and azoles, the interest to which is constantly 
increasing. The combination of a ferrocene and a pyrrole ring sys- 
tems in a one molecule leads to the structures, even more in- 
teresting and promising, especially in the ﬁelds of organic syn- 
thesis, asymmetric catalysis, electrochemistry, materials science, 
biomedical research, and so on [3] , than each of them separately. 
Some of pyrrole-ferrocene ensembles, in which ferrocene and pyr- 
role systems are bonded directly [4] or joined via a spacer, such 
as a methylene, carbonyl, amido, amidoalkyl, phosphine groups 
that separate the two ring systems [5] , are described in the lit- 
erature. Most of the known approaches to such ensembles are 
based on functionalization of preexisting pyrrole rings (unsubsti- 
tuted or substituted) with ferrocene derivatives [ 3 c −e, 4 a −c, 5 b,c]. 
The pyrrole-ferrocene ensembles were also accessed via con- 
struction of ferrocene ring system (starting from cyclopenta-1,3- 
dienyl-substituted pyrroles) [ 5 e] and via construction of pyrrole

ring (starting from suitable ferrocene derivatives) [ 4 d,e]. However, 
methods for the synthesis of ferrocenyl-substituted pyrroles were 
rather limited. 
(Alkylsulfanyl)pyrroles, displaying a broad spectrum of applica- 
tions [6] , are also attractive targets of great current interest as im- 
portant organosulfur compounds as hetaryl sulﬁdes [7] that are en- 
dowed with high reactivity, and properties valuable for pharmacol- 
ogy, optoelectronic and hi-tech materials. Among the known meth- 
ods for the synthesis of multisubstituted 2-(alkylsulfanyl) −1 H - 
pyrroles from acyclic precursors [8] , the methodology using isoth- 
iocyanates both as a structural fragment of pyrrole core and sup- 
plier of the sulfur atom for sulfa-substituents, along with allenes 
or alkynes (as supplier of three carbon atoms for pyrrole ring 
and substituents for 3 and/or 5 positions), seems to be the most 
powerful, simple and perspective. Thus, the combination of differ- 
ent isothiocyanates with allenic or acetylenic carbanions, generated 
in situ from the corresponding allenes or alkynes, affords di- or 
trisubstituted 2-(alkylsulfanyl)pyrroles in good to excellent yields 
in one preparative step [ 9 , 10 ]. 
Nevertheless, pyrroles bearing ferrocenylalkoxy substituent or 
both ferrocene and alkylsulfanyl moieties, to the best of our knowl- 
edge, have not been hitherto described, but exactly from such 
pyrroles one might expect some novel interesting and unique 
properties aside from known very useful own properties of 
pyrroles, ferrocenes, and sulﬁdes.

Consequently, synthesis of ferrocenyl-substituted 2- 
(alkylsulfanyl)pyrroles is a challenging task, especially in the 
synthetic strategies based on available starting materials. 
To initiate our study, we have synthesized the ferrocenic ana- 
logue of methoxyallene, i.e., (ferrocenylmethoxy)allene ( 1 ) [11] , as 
a new building block and supplier of ferrocene functions for the 
one-pot synthesis of 3-(ferrocenylmethoxy) −2-sulfanyl-1 H -pyrroles 
2 . 
2. Results and discussion 
2.1. Synthesis of 3-(ferrocenylmethoxy) −2-sulfanyl-1H-pyrroles 2 
New ferrocene-substituted pyrroles 2a –i were synthesized in 
one preparative step, according to our novel general approach to 
the pyrrole ring construction from isothiocyanates and allenes or 
alkynes [ 9 , 10 ], namely by the reaction of α-lithiated (ferrocenyl- 
methoxy)allene ( 3 ) with isothiocyanate followed by the consec- 
utive S-alkylation of adduct 4 and Cu(I)-catalyzed intramolecular 
[1,5]-cyclization of the forming alkyl allenylimidothioate (1-aza- 
1,3,4-triene 5 ) ( Table 1 ). 
Lithiation of (ferrocenylmethoxy)allene ( 1 ) was carried out 
with n -BuLi in THF/hexane at −100 → −65 to −40 °C 
for 5 − 15 min. Temperature and time of the interaction 
of 1-(ferrocenylmethoxy) −1-lithioallene ( 3 ) with isothiocyanate 
( Table 1 , Scheme, step ii) depends on structure of the latter. Thus, 
the complete addition of lithioallene 3 to methyl isothiocyanate oc- 
curs at −50 to −40 °C for 5 − 10 min, to 2-(vinyloxy)ethyl and 
phenyl isothiocyanates –a t −45 to −40 °C for 10 min and at ca. 
−65 °C for 15 min, respectively. Addition of lithioallene 3 to sec- 
ondary isothiocyanates, such as isopropyl, cyclopentyl, and cyclo- 
heptyl ones, was carried out at ca. −30 °C for 20 min. The forming 
lithium buta-2,3-dienimidothioates 4 were alkylated on the sul- 
fur atom with methyl iodide, propargyl and benzyl bromides at 
−80 → −10 to −5 °C. The higher temperature for alkylation is not 
required because undesirable in this case isomerization (via [1,5]- 
H shift) of 1-aza-1,3,4-trienes 5 into conjugated 2-aza-1,3,5-trienes 
(precursors of 2,3-dihydropyridines) [ 9 c, 12 ] can take place (for N- 
Alk and N-cycloAlk derivatives). Addition of CuBr or CuI to the re- 
action mixture at low temperature (ca. −10 to −5 °С ) followed by 
heating at 30 −50 °C for 15 −50 min led to intramolecular cycliza- 
tion of 1-aza-1,3,4-triene 5 into pyrrole ring 2 . 
The use of propargyl bromide as an alkylating agent (instead of 
methyl iodide) in the studied reaction (for example, with methyl 
isothiocyanate) resulted in 2-(prop–2-ynylsulfanyl) −1 H -pyrrole 2 h 
containing an additional reaction center ( Table 1 ). Similar reac- 
tion with benzyl bromide led to the corresponding benzylsulfanyl 
derivative 2i . 
However, when alkyl bromoacetates were used as alkylating 
agents, modiﬁcation of the reaction conditions was required. It was 
necessary in order to switch the 1-aza-1,3,4-trienes 5j,k cycliza- 
tion from the corresponding thiophenes 6 to pyrroles 2 ( Scheme 1 ) 
[13] . This occurred when the 1-aza-1,3,4-trienes 5j,k were prelim- 
inary isolated from the reaction mixture and then subjected to 
the action of CuBr (~9.0 mol%). Otherwise, i.e., when the reaction 
was carried out in one preparative step (as shown in Table 1 and 
Scheme 1 ), the formed in situ 1-aza-1,3,4-trienes 5 , bearing sul- 
fanylacetate substituent, very rapidly cyclized to the corresponding 
alkyl 5-aminothiophene-2-carboxylates 6 [14] . 
In order to suppress the rapid cyclization of the 1-aza-1,3,4- 
trienes 5j,k to corresponding thiophenes 6 , prior to the S- 
alkylation of the adducts 4j,k ( Table 1 ), one equivalent of water 
was added to the reaction mixture, and the treatment with alkyl 
bromoacetates was carried out at a lower temperature, namely at 
−80 to −30 °C for 10 mins (instead of −80 to 15 °C for 15 min) 
( Scheme 1 ).

Importantly, all these syntheses are scalable, and have been 
readily implemented on a gram scale. Non-optimized yields of

2-(benzylsulfanyl)-substituted pyrroles 2 g, 2 h , and 2i , are crys-

2 h , and 2i are viscous liquids. The structures of the products have 
been assigned using 1 H, 13 C, and heteronuclear 2D ( 1 H, 13 C HSQC, 
1 H, 13 C and 1 H, 15 N HMBC) NMR and IR spectroscopy and mass- 
spectrometry. The molecular structure of pyrrole 2f has been de- 
termined by X-ray diffraction ( Fig. 1 ).

2.2. Formal [1,3]-O-to-C-rearrangement of 
3-(ferrocenylmethoxy) −2-sulfanyl-1H-pyrroles 2 into 
2-(ferrocenylmethyl) −2-sulfanyl-1,2-dihydro-3H-pyrrol-3-ones 7 
It was noticed that during storage of a solution of pyrroles 
2a −k in CDCl 3 at room temperature, their color was changed 
in time from yellow-orange to dark-brown. Repeated NMR spec- 
tra of these samples recorded after 2 to 57 days (or 4.5 and 
4 months for pyrroles 2j and 2k , respectively) showed that 
3-(ferrocenylmethoxy) −2-sulfanyl-1 H -pyrroles 2 partially or fully 
transformed into previously unknown 2-(ferrocenylmethyl) −2- 
sulfanyl-1,2-dihydro-3 H -pyrrol-3-ones 7 ( Table 2 ). 
It is important to note, that although pyrroles 2 have a struc- 
tural fragment (highlighted in red), which with a certain degree 
of conditionality can be attributed to allyl vinyl ( 8 ) or allyl aryl 
( 9 ) ethers, unlike the latter [18] , they are not exposed to classical 
Claisen rearrangement (under the above conditions) with the for- 
mation of 1,2-dihydro-3 H -pyrrol-3-ones 10 and/or 11 ( Scheme 2 ). 
On the other hand, earlier unknown 3-allyloxy-2- 
(methylsulfanyl) −1-phenyl-1 H -pyrrole ( 12a ) and 3-benzyloxy-2- 
(methylsulfanyl) −1-phenyl-1 H -pyrrole ( 12b ), specially synthesized 
from allyloxy- and benzyloxyallenes, phenyl isothiocyanate and 
methyl iodide (via CuBr-catalyzed cyclization of 1-aza-1,3,4-trienes 
13 ), the most closest (by structure) analogues of pyrrole 2f and 
allyl hetaryl ethers, under the similar conditions (CDCl 3 , r.t., ~20 
days) did not rearrange into the corresponding 1,2-dihydro-3 H - 
pyrrol-3-ones 14 ( Scheme 3 ), the ferrocenylmethoxy-substituted 
analogue 2f being rearranged quantitatively ( Table 2 ). 
Products of the Claisen rearrangement of pyrroles 12 , i.e., 1,2- 
dihydro-3 H -pyrrol-3-ones 14a and 15b or 16b , were also not iden- 
tiﬁed ( Scheme 4 ). Starting materials were recovered.

Thus, it becomes obvious that the ability of the pyrroles 
2 to a rearrange into 1,2-dihydro-3 H -pyrrol-3-ones 7 , moreover 
under such mild conditions, is provided by the speciﬁc effect 
of ferrocene fragment. According to the propensity to rearrange 
into 1,2-dihydro-3 H -pyrrol-3-ones 7 under comparable conditions 
(CDCl 3 , r.t., 19 −21 days), pyrroles 2 stand in the following or- 
der ( Table 2 ): 2f (R 1 = Ph, 100%) > 2a (R 1 = Me, ~96%) > 2c 
(R 1 = CH 2 = CHOCH 2 CH 2 , 77%) > 2e (R 1 = cycloC 7 H 13 , 21%). Pyrrole 
2i (R 2 = Bn) quantitatively rearranges into 1,2-dihydro-3 H -pyrrol- 
3-one 7i after 16 days. While, pyrrole 2l (R 2 = CH 2 CN) did not 
show a tendency to rearrange into 1,2-dihydro-3 H -pyrrol-3-one 7l , 
when its solution in CDCl 3 was stored at room temperature for 14 
days (analyzed by 1 H NMR). In the case of pyrrole 2 g , on the 
contrary, the rearrangement into 1,2-dihydro-3 H -pyrrol-3-one 7 g 
occurs already when it is puriﬁed by column chromatography on 
neutral alumina ( Table 2 ). 
On the basis of the structure of the products obtained, which is 
conﬁrmed by NMR spectra, it is possible to assume, that transfor- 
mation of 3-(ferrocenylmethoxy) −1 H -pyrroles 2 into 1,2-dihydro- 
3 H -pyrrol-3-ones 7 occurs through the so-called «formal [1,3]-O- 
to-C rearrangement», a relatively rare type of rearrangements (pre- 
dominantly in the range of allyl aryl ethers and hetarylmethyl vinyl 
ethers) [19] . The pyrrole ring is involved in this rearrangement 
as the vinyl ether component, whereas the ferrocenylmethyl sub- 
stituent participates as the “allylic” counterpart. It should be em- 
phasized that so far the rearrangements of this type among the 
pyrrole derivatives were not observed. It was also shown, that 
some other heteroaromatics, for instance, 1,3-oxazole [ 19 h], fu- 
ran, and thiophene [ 19 i], participate as the vinyl ether compo- 
nent in the thermal (xylene, 120 °C, 3 h) [1,3]-O-to-C rearrange- 
ment of 5-(benzyloxy) −1,3-oxazoles and 2-(benzyloxy)furans and 
-thiophenes. 
One of possible routes of the found rearrangement of pyrroles 
2 , similarly to the published rearrangements of this type [19] , 
includes a tandem O[1,3]-sigmatropic shift (through intermediate 
A with a conﬁguration inversion of the oxygen atom) and [3,3]- 
sigmatropic shift (the Claisen rearrangement) in the intermediate 
B (via intermediate C ) ( Scheme 5 ). 
However, most of the known examples of the formal [1,3]-O- 
to-C migration, occurring via the depicted in Scheme 5 plausible 
mechanism, belong to the thermally induced rearrangements [ 19 a], 
whereas the rearrangement found by us is implemented at room 
temperature and is initiated, apparently, by HCl, presented in deu- 
terium chloroform in trace amounts (see Table 2 ). 
It can be also assumed that the transformation of pyrroles 2 
into 1,2-dihydro-3 H -pyrrol-3-ones 7 occurs through the catalytic or 
heterolytic carbon–oxygen bond cleavage [20] , which leads to fairly 
stable ferrocenylmethyl carbocation D and pyrrolyloxide anions E 
( Scheme 6 ). The subsequent interaction between the carbocation D

The presence in the mass spectra of pyrroles 2 of the peak of 
an ion with a mass of 199 of maximum intensity, [FcCH 2 ] + (100%), 
serves as an additional conﬁrmation of the ease of cleavage of the 
C –O bond leading to the formation of the stable ferrocenylmethyl 
carbocation D ( Scheme 6 ). 
The proposed mechanism of the rearrangement of 2 → 7 in 
CDCl 3 (via ferrocenylmethyl carbocation) is also supported by the 
literature data [ 19 d, 19 i, 20 a, 20 b]. Thus, [1,3]-benzyl group migration 
from oxygen to carbon in CDCl 3 (r.t., 6 − 8 weeks) was observed 
for 2-furylbenzyl ethers [ 19 i]. 2-Furylmethyl and 2-thienylmethyl 
vinyl ethers in medium of lithium perchlorate in diethyl ether (r.t., 
6 h) were smoothly transformed to the formal [1,3]-rearrangement 
products, γ-heteroaryl propanals [ 19 d]. In contrast, benzyl and 
naphthylmethyl vinyl ethers exhibited the inertness under simi- 
lar conditions. Formation of rather stable ferrocenylmethyl carbo- 
cations under very mild conditions (through heterolytic cleavage of 
the C –O bond in α-ferrocenylalkyl carbonates) and their participa- 
tion in ferrocenylalkylation reactions was also described [ 20 a, 20 b]. 
We have also tested the ability of pyrroles 2 to thermally- 
induced rearrangement into 1,2-dihydro-3H-pyrrol-3-ones 7 
( Scheme 5 ) or 10 / 11 ( Scheme 2 ). For this, a solution of pyrrole 
2f in toluene was heated at 98 −100 °C for several hours. The 
course of the reaction was monitored by 1 H NMR spectra. It 
turned out that, after 3 h, the conversion of pyrrole 2f into

2.3. Transformation of 
N-[2-(vinyloxy)ethyl] −3-(ferrocenylmethoxy) −1H-pyrrole 2c into 
N-vinylpyrrole 17 
Recently, we have established that 3–methoxy-analogue of pyr- 
role 2c , prepared from lithiated methoxyallene, 2-(vinyloxy)ethyl 
isothiocyanate and MeI, by treatment with 
t -BuOK/DMSO can be easily converted into the 3–methoxy- 
2-(methylsulfanyl)- N -vinylpyrrole [ 10 b]. The involvement of 3- 
(ferrocenylmethoxy)pyrrole 2c in the reaction with 
t -BuOK/DMSO also gave N -vinylpyrrole, namely 3- 
(ferrocenylmethoxy) −2-(methylsulfanyl) −1-vinyl-1 H -pyrrole ( 17 ) 
in a yield of 96%. The reaction proceeds at r.t. for ~30 min via 
elimination of vinyl alcohol from the N -[2-(vinyloxy)ethyl] sub- 
stituent and represents a novel approach to ferrocenyl-substituted 
N -vinylpyrroles ( Scheme 7 ). 
N -Vinylpyrrole 17 , like pyrroles 2 , in CDCl 3 solution rearranges 
into 1,2-dihydro-3 H -pyrrol-3-one 18 ( Scheme 8 ). 
3. Conclusion 
We have described a one- and two-pot assembly of 3- 
(ferrocenylmethoxy) −2-sulfanyl-1 H -pyrroles from readily ac- 
cessible starting materials, lithiated (ferrocenylmethoxy)allene, 
isothiocyanates, and alkylating agents. The reaction proceeds 
via synthesis and Cu(I)-catalyzed intramolecular cyclization of 
alkyl 2-(ferrocenylmethoxy)buta-2,3-dienimidothioates (1-aza- 
1,3,4-trienes), which serve as the key intermediates in this 
approach. Although the non-optimized isolated yields of the target 
products were from moderate to good (18–67%), the presented 
approach allows direct synthesis of 3-(ferrocenylmethoxy) −2- 
sulfanyl-1 H -pyrroles as promising basic compounds for the 
design of new generations of molecular sensors, ferromag- 
nets, catalysts, optoelectronic materials, drugs, and diagnos- 
tic tools for medicine. An unexpected rearrangement of the 
synthesized 3-(ferrocenylmethoxy) −2-sulfanyl-1 H -pyrroles into 
2-(ferrocenylmethyl) −2-sulfanyl-1,2-dihydro-3 H -pyrrol-3-ones, oc- 
curring at room temperature in CDCl 3 or when heated in toluene, 
has been discovered. On the basis of experimental and literature 
data it is assumed that the rearrangement proceeds through two 
different mechanisms of activation of the formal [1,3]-O-to-C- 
migration of ferrocenylmethyl group: 1) via acid-mediated process 
with generation of ferrocenylmethyl carbocation (in CDCl 3 ) or 2) 
via tandem O[1,3]-sigmatropic shift and Claisen rearrangement 
(under heating). Although pyrroles 2 can be classiﬁed as Claisen 
systems, no [3,3]-sigmatropic process was observed, in all cases. 
4. Experimental 
4.1. General 
(Ferrocenylmethoxy)allene ( 1 ) was synthesized using the 
method reported earlier [11] . Isopropyl, 2-(vinyloxy)ethyl, cy- 
clopentyl, and cycloheptyl isothiocyanates were obtained accord- 
ing to our procedure from primary amines, carbon disulﬁde and 
acetyl chloride [ 9 a, 21 a] or acetic anhydride [ 9 a, 21 b]. (Allyloxy)- 
and (benzyloxy)allenes were prepared as described in literature 
[22] . Methyl and phenyl isothiocyanates, n -BuLi (1.6, 2.37, and

To a vigorously stirred solution of (ferrocenylmethoxy)allene ( 1 ) 
(10.0 − 15.0 mmol) in dry THF (20 −40 mL), n -BuLi (6 − 11 mL 
of 1.6, 2.37, and 2.5 M solutions in hexane, 15.0 − 17.6 mmol) 
was added at −100 to −90 °C under argon. After stirring for an 
additional 5 − 15 min at ca. −65 to −40 °C, the solution was 
cooled to ca. −90 to −70 °C and a mixture of isothiocyanate 
(10.0 − 15.0 mmol) and THF (3 − 5 mL) was added in one por- 
tion. After being stirred for 5 − 10 min at −50 to −40 °C (for 
methyl isothiocyanate), for 20 min at ca. −30 °C (for iso and cy- 
cloalkyl isothiocyanates), for 10 min at −45 to −40 °C [for 2- 
(vinyloxy)ethyl isothiocyanate] and for 15 min at ca. −65 °C (for 
phenyl isothiocyanate), the mixture was again cooled to ca. −80 °C 
and methyl iodide (22.9 − 35.7 mmol, 1.5 − 2.4 equiv) or propar- 
gyl bromide (18.5 mmol, 1.2 equiv) or benzyl bromide (10.0 mmol, 
1.0 equiv) were added in one portion. The cooling bath was re- 
moved, and when the temperature was reached −10 to −5 °C, CuI 
(2.10 −3.15 mmol) was added. The reaction mixture was stirred for 
15 −50 min at 32 −50 °C, then cooled to r.t. and treated with sat- 
urated aqueous NH 4 Cl solution (30 mL) contained NaCN (0.50 g). 
The layers were separated, and the aqueous phase was extracted 
with Et 2 O (3 × 30 mL). The organic layers were combined, washed 
with H 2 O (50 mL), dried (MgSO 4 ), and concentrated under reduced 
pressure to give a residue consisting of corresponding pyrrole 2 (by 
1 H NMR). Pure compounds 2a –2i were isolated by column chro- 
matography on neutral alumina, using hexane and hexane/Et 2 O as 
eluent. Yields (based on isothiocyanate) and characteristic data of 
pyrroles 2a –2i are reported below.

preparative steps, namely, with the isolation of the corresponding 
1-aza-1,3,4-triene 5 followed by its cyclization into pyrrole in the 
presence of CuBr. If the reaction was carried out in one preparative 
stage, i.e., the catalyst was added to the reaction mixture contain- 
ing in situ generated 1-aza-1,3,4-triene 5j or 5k , then, instead of 
the expected pyrroles 2j and 2k , the corresponding thiophenes 6j 
and 6k were obtained [14] . 
During storage of a solutions of pyrroles 2a −k in CDCl 3 
at room temperature their rearrangement (partial or complete) 
into 2-(ferrocenylmethyl) −2-sulfanyl-1,2-dihydro-3 H -pyrrol-3-ones 
7 ( Table 2 ) was observed (by 1 H NMR spectra). The TLC analysis 
indicated that R f values of products 2 and 7 are very close and dif- 
ﬁcult to separate by column chromatography. When the reaction 
was conducted in toluene at 98 −100 °C for 8 h, pyrrole 2f is al- 
most quantitatively converted into 1,2-dihydro-3 H -pyrrol-3-one 7f .
